gallery.title: Semiconducting Thin films and Fabrication Workshop- PSG IAS
gallery.description: The workshop focused on Thin Film Characterization Techniques, beginning with a session on "Materials Characterization Techniques" by Dr. Anuradha Ashok, followed by "Thin Film Characterization" by Dr. Sebin Devasia. Participants also attended an expert lecture on "New Materials Design for Quantum Technologies and Neuromorphic Devices and Computation" delivered by Prof. Ramesh Thamankar from the Centre for Functional Materials, VIT Vellore. The day concluded with an interactive hands-on session on materials characterization, providing practical exposure to advanced characterization tools and analysis techniques.

gallery.title: Clean Room Facilities- PSG IAS, Coimbatore
gallery.description: We explored "Thin Film Devices in Microelectronics and MEMS" with Dr. Geetha Priyadarshini Badhirappan, followed by "Thin Film Deposition Techniques (Physical & Chemical)" by Dr. Veena M..   The highlight of the day was an expert lecture by Dr Parthasarathy Srinivasan (Amrita School of Engineering, Chennai) on "Advanced Thin Film Deposition: From Lab-Scale to Industrial Fabrication."   The afternoon concluded with an engaging hands-on session on thin-film deposition.

researchAreas.title: Dye Sensitized Solar Cells
researchAreas.description: My  Research work is mainly focused on investigating alternative materials for counter electrodes in DSSCs. Specifically, the use of metal sulfides prepared through hydrothermal sulfurization as alternatives to conventional platinum-based electrodes was explored. Through a combination of experimental synthesis, characterization, and device fabrication, I successfully demonstrated the feasibility of these metal sulfides for enhancing DSSC performance

researchAreas.title: Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
researchAreas.description: EIS technique gives enormous information about the interfaces by modelling circuit for the respective Electrode / Electrolyte interface. i love this technique which is very useful to study the charge carrier dynamics at the interfaces.

researchAreas.title: Electrochemical Techniques
researchAreas.description: Electrochemical techniques especially Metrohm Autolab is my favorite workstation in which i can analyze, automate and calculate my data. The best thing in Metrohm is the NOVA software that allows us to customize the program order and schedule it.

researchAreas.title: Ion Beam Irradiation
researchAreas.description:
I have irradiated and studied  my samples using Ion beam implantation (LEIBF & SNICS) at IUAC, New Delhi. and found tremendous improvement in light absorption. i began my research as project fellow in IUAC sponsored Project at NIT Silchar under the guidance of Dr. Ranjith G Nair, 

Moreover i worked on Gamma Irradiation, during my PhD  (under guidance of Dr. B. Muthuraaman) period at University of Madras we found that gamma irradiaiton improved the DSSC performance

researchAreas.title: Thin film deposition
researchAreas.description: During my IUAC project, i worked on Physical Vapor Deposition methods such as RF sputtering to prepare TiO2 thin films with various thickness. Moreover i have hands on experience on Thermal Evaporation, E-Beam, Spray and Spin coating techniques to fabricate thin films

researchAreas.title: Photo-electrochemical Studies
researchAreas.description:
I performed photoelectrochemical studies for the photocatalyst samples which was prepared by Ranjith G Nair Research group and found the materials are performed superior under light conditions.

Photoelectrochemical studies examine how light interacts with materials—usually semiconductors placed in a liquid—to turn solar energy into electricity or clean chemical fuels. These methods focus on core processes like light absorption, charge separation, and surface reactions
